meta.title: Siaya budget transparency and public participation: IBP Kenya CBTS 2021 and 2022, APRM Siaya County Review Report 2024
meta.rule: Each edition is kept separate; no score is carried forward from one edition to another. Every item carries source_id, page, edition and year. Findings are attributed to the publishing body, quoted briefly, with no verdicts. No individuals are named; offices only. Aggregates only (docs/data-protection-policy.md).
meta.page_convention: page_pdf is the 1-based page in the PDF file whose SHA-256 is given under sources; page_printed is the number printed on the page where there is one.

ibp_cbts.method_note: The CBTS checks whether ten key budget documents that the PFM Act requires counties to publish are available on the county's official website, then scores the comprehensiveness of the content of those found (revenue, expenditure, budget performance, non-financial information, public participation). The transparency index is out of 100. Public participation is evaluated only in three documents: Annual Development Plan, County Fiscal Strategy Paper and Approved Programme Based Budget.

aprm.method_note: A County Peer Review Mechanism report led by the county's research team with the NEPAD/APRM Kenya Secretariat: desk review of county documents 2013-2022, focus group discussions in all wards (24-25 July 2023), self-assessment questionnaires to County Assembly and executive offices, analysis with KNBS, and sub-county validation (April 2024). The 'County progress report' sections are the county's own account; 'Key findings' and 'Areas of concern' come from the engagements.

findings.quote: the performance of Siaya County in the function of public participation promotion was generally higher compared to all other functions
findings.also: Areas needing improvement listed as 'institutional frameworks, feedback mechanisms, reporting and funding of public participation'.

findings.section: 3.14 b) County progress report (county's own account)
findings.quote: enacted the Public Participation (PP) and Petitions Act, 2015; established and operationalized the Public Participation and Petitions directorate
findings.also: Reports regular public forums since 2013, mainly at ward level; digital channels; draft public participation guidelines; sign language interpreters at forums.

findings.section: 3.14 b) County progress report (county's own account)
findings.quote: captured on the Complaint register which tracks handling until dispensed

findings.quote: 48 civic education sessions were conducted in FY 2018/2029
findings.note: '2018/2029' is printed as such [sic]; the intended year is not stated. Conducted with civil society partners named in the report.

findings.section: 3.14 c) Key findings from county engagements
findings.measure: Ward perception score, promotion of public participation
findings.quote: a majority of the wards (27 wards) scored above 5 out of 10
findings.note: Text cites 'Figure 11'; the chart below it is captioned 'Figure 17'. Perception scores from focus groups, not a measured outcome.

findings.quote: there are often low turnouts at public participation forums
findings.also: Attributed in the report to expectation of fare reimbursement, lack of awareness, apathy or mistrust.

findings.quote: There is a gap in civic education and awareness-raising initiatives
There was a lack of operational civic education programme notably curriculum, training manual/module, and IEC materials
faced resource constraints that limited their ability to effectively engage citizens
findings.also: Refers to the county's public participation directorate and to civil society organisations.

findings.quote: There was a general perception that public input was not adequately considered in final governmental decisions
were weak and lacked effectiveness and were, therefore, underutilized
findings.also: Refers to public forums, ward development committees and participatory budgeting.

findings.quote: Lack of county public participation policy, guidelines, non-establishment of citizen participation framework/structures
Lack of transparent and accessible information about county government activities, policies, and decision-making processes as required by law was observed.
There are limited feedback mechanisms for citizens to provide feedback on government decisions, policies, and services
CSOs in Siaya County have sometimes faced challenges from county government authorities, including bureaucratic hurdles and political interference
findings.note: A finding attributed to the report; it names no office or person and gives no cases. Not verified by Takwimu.

findings.quote: only a small number of citizens at the local level access the newspapers
findings.also: Context: announcements for participation sessions are made in newspapers.

findings.quote: Establish County Citizen Participation Structures/Committees at all levels and feedback mechanism
findings.also: Other recommendations: a county public participation policy and amendment of the 2015 Act; a civic education curriculum, manual and materials; documents provided 'preferably 7 working days prior'; participation from village level; announcements on local and vernacular radio.

caveats: Survey timing: each CBTS edition checks county websites at a point after the fiscal year it covers. A document posted after the check counts as not published. The 2021 edition says the county made five more documents public after seeing draft results (IBP-02 p.78), so the round's final figures may reflect documents published in response to the survey.
Editions are not merged. The 2022 edition reprints earlier-round figures; these are kept inside the 2022 block and marked as reprinted, not used to fill the 2021 block.
IBP-01 p.1 prints '70/100' beside the heading 'How comprehensive is the content of budget documents'; its meaning is not explained on the page, so it is not recorded as a score.
The APRM report is a self-assessment process run by the county with the APRM Secretariat; 'County progress report' text is the county's own account. Ward scores are perceptions from focus groups.
APRM-01 p.4 dates the finalisation workshop 'April 15th to 19th, 2014', which is inconsistent with the 2023-2024 timeline; recorded as printed, not used.
